videos.title: Dating Coach: The #1 Sign He’ll Actually Stay with You | Jillian Turecki
videos.description:
Weeks of texting someone feels like intimacy. It's actually the safest way to never get rejected.

In this clip, Jillian Turecki and Jay Shetty talk about the three mistakes people keep making in dating, and why the fourth one, the month-long text thread with a stranger, might be the most expensive of all.

Jillian breaks down why we chase the people who don't want us and lose interest in the ones who do, what "chemistry" is actually measuring, and why the person you pick matters more than almost any other decision you'll make. Jay shares the friend who came back from a perfect date and didn't want a second one.

Learn about the difference between a spark and a value, why your 16-year-old self is still running your dating life, and the one piece of advice from a therapist that Jillian calls the worst she's ever received.

JAY'S DAILY WISDOM DELIVERED STRAIGHT TO YOUR INBOX
Join 900,000+ readers discovering how small daily shifts create big life change with my free newsletter. Subscribe https://news.jayshetty.me/subscribe

You've been told your whole life to explore, keep your options open, try new things. And you've done exactly that. Moved cities, pivoted careers, taken every personality quiz. But here's what nobody warns you about: all that freedom might be the thing keeping you stuck.
This episode digs into a depressed 19th century Danish philosopher who diagnosed our entire modern crisis 180 years before we lived it. We tell the story of Casanova, history's most famous fuckboy, who had more adventures than anyone alive and died completely alone with nothing but 2,000 pages of memories nobody believed. We break down Dan Gilbert's research on why your brain is actually better at justifying your choices than you give it credit for. We walk through Kierkegaard's three stages of commitment, from the aesthetic life of endless options to the point where commitment stops feeling like a choice at all. And we talk about the grief that nobody tells you about when you finally pick one life and let all the others go.
